((w+h)²-w²)/h = 2w+h: The difference between w plus h squared and w squared, divided by h, equals two w plus h.
(2.2-.6)/.8=2: Two point two minus zero point six, divided by zero point eight, equals two.
(f(w+h)-f(w-h))/(2h): The function at w plus h minus the function at w minus h, all divided by two h.
(positive_count+1)/(leaf_count+2): The positive count plus one, divided by the leaf count plus two.
(substitutions+deletions+insertions)/ref: The total substitutions, deletions and insertions, divided by the number of reference words.
(tenant,operation_id): The pair consisting of tenant and operation identifier.
(wx-y)^2/2: One half of the squared difference between w times x and y.
(wx-y)x: The quantity w times x minus y, multiplied by x.
(wx-y)x+lambda*w: The quantity w times x minus y, multiplied by x, plus lambda times w.
(x·y)/(||x|| ||y||): The dot product of x and y divided by the product of their Euclidean norms.
-(log(.5)+log(.25)+log(.8))/3≈.768: The negative sum of the natural logarithms of zero point five, zero point two five and zero point eight, divided by three, is approximately zero point seven six eight.
-(log(.8)+log(.7))/2≈.289909: The negative sum of the natural logarithms of zero point eight and zero point seven, divided by two, is approximately zero point two eight nine nine zero nine.
-[y log p+(1-y) log(1-p)]: The negative of y times the natural logarithm of p, plus one minus y times the natural logarithm of one minus p.
-log(sigmoid(m)): The negative natural logarithm of the sigmoid of margin m.
.09/(.09+.09)=.5: Zero point zero nine divided by the sum of zero point zero nine and zero point zero nine equals zero point five.
0.1+0.2 == 0.3: Whether zero point one plus zero point two is exactly equal to zero point three in computer arithmetic.
1-.95^20≈.642: One minus zero point nine five raised to the twentieth power is approximately zero point six four two.
1-sum_k p_k²: One minus the sum of squared class probabilities.
2 L T H_kv d b: Two times the number of layers, times sequence length, times the number of key-value heads, times head width, times bytes per stored number.
2(N-1)S/N: Two times N minus one, times S, divided by N.
2*3 + 1*(-1) = 5: Two times three plus one times negative one equals five.
20p > 1(1-p): Twenty times probability p is greater than one times the quantity one minus p.
C_ij=mean(centered_x_i*centered_x_j): Covariance entry C sub i j is the mean product of centered coordinate i and centered coordinate j.
DeltaW=BA: The weight update delta W equals matrix B times matrix A.
E[(X-E[X])²]: The expected squared difference between X and its expectation.
E[X]=sum_x x P(X=x): The expectation of X is the sum over possible values x of x times the probability that X equals x.
FF(h)=ReLU(h I) I: The feed-forward output is the rectified linear activation of h times the identity matrix, multiplied by the identity matrix again.
H(P)=-sum_x P(x) log P(x): Entropy of P is the negative sum over outcomes x of P of x times the natural logarithm of P of x.
H(P,Q)=-sum_x P(x) log Q(x): Cross-entropy from P to Q is the negative sum over x of P of x times the natural logarithm of Q of x.
J(theta)=(1/n)sum_i L(f_theta(x_i),y_i): The objective J of theta is the mean, over n examples, of the loss between the model prediction for each input and its target.
J=(wx-y)²/2: The objective J is one half of the squared difference between w times x and y.
J_reg=J+(lambda/2)||w||²: The regularized objective is J plus lambda divided by two times the squared Euclidean norm of the weights.
KL(P||Q)=sum_x P(x) log(P(x)/Q(x)): K L divergence from P to Q sums, over x, P of x times the natural logarithm of the ratio P of x to Q of x.
LN(r)=(r-mean(r))/sqrt(mean((r-mean(r))²: Layer normalization subtracts the mean of vector r, then divides by the square root of its mean squared centered deviation plus epsilon.
N=lambda*W: N equals arrival rate lambda times average time W.
P(A and B)=P(A)P(B): The probability of both A and B equals the probability of A times the probability of B.
P(A|B)=P(A and B)/P(B): The probability of A given B equals the probability of both A and B divided by the probability of B.
P(A|B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B): The probability of A given B equals the probability of B given A, times the probability of A, divided by the probability of B.
P(b|a)=(count(a,b)+alpha)/(count(a)+alph: The conditional probability of token b given a is the count of that pair plus alpha, divided by the count of a plus alpha times vocabulary size V.
P(fault|positive)≈.0833: The probability of a fault given a positive result is approximately zero point zero eight three three.
P(positive|fault)=.9: The probability of a positive result given a fault is zero point nine.
P(t1,...,tT)=product_i P(t_i|t_<i): The joint probability of a token sequence is the product of each token probability conditioned on all preceding tokens.
W2(W1x+b1)+b2=(W2W1)x+(W2b1+b2): Applying two affine layers without a nonlinear activation gives a single affine layer: the combined weight is W two times W one, and the combined bias is W two times b one plus b two.
XᵀXw=Xᵀy: X transposed times X times w equals X transposed times y.
[lo,w,_]: the tokens l o, w, and a word-boundary marker
[low,_]: the token low and a word-boundary marker
[low,e,r,_]: the tokens low, e, r, and a word-boundary marker
a_j=tanh(sum_k W1_jk x_k+b1_j): Hidden activation a sub j is the hyperbolic tangent of the sum over k of first-layer weight j k times input k, plus hidden bias j.
dL/dW1_jk=delta*v_j*(1-a_j²)*x_k: The loss derivative for first-layer weight j k is delta times output weight j, times one minus hidden activation j squared, times input k.
dL/db1_j=delta*v_j*(1-a_j²): The loss derivative for hidden bias j is delta times output weight j times one minus hidden activation j squared.
dL/db2=delta: The loss derivative for the output bias equals delta.
dL/dv_j=delta*a_j: The loss derivative for output weight j equals delta times hidden activation j.
dL/dw=(dL/dz)(dz/dw): The derivative of loss with respect to w is the derivative of loss with respect to z times the derivative of z with respect to w.
dL/dw=(p-y)x: The derivative of loss with respect to w is predicted probability p minus target y, multiplied by input x.
dL/dz=p-y: The derivative of loss with respect to logit z is predicted probability p minus target y.
exp(a+b)=exp(a)exp(b): The exponential of a plus b equals the exponential of a times the exponential of b.
f_theta(x): the function with parameters theta applied to input x
h=phi(Wx+b): Hidden representation h equals activation function phi applied to W times x plus b.
h_t=tanh(x_t+.5*h_(t-1)): The hidden state at time t is the hyperbolic tangent of current input x plus one half of the previous hidden state.
idf(t)*tf*(k1+1)/(tf+k1*(1-b+b*length(d): The score multiplies inverse document frequency by term frequency times k one plus one, then divides by term frequency plus k one times the length-adjustment factor. That factor is one minus b plus b times document length divided by average document length.
idf(t)=log(1+(N-df(t)+.5)/(df(t)+.5)): Inverse document frequency is the natural logarithm of one plus the ratio of N minus document frequency plus one half, to document frequency plus one half.
log(ab)=log(a)+log(b): The natural logarithm of a times b equals the natural logarithm of a plus the natural logarithm of b.
m=beta*(log(pi(chosen)/pi_ref(chosen))-l: The margin m is beta times the chosen response log probability ratio between policy and reference, minus the corresponding log probability ratio for the rejected response.
mean((p-y)²): the mean squared difference between predicted probability p and observed target y
n≈2*(1.96+.84)²*.25/delta²: The approximate sample size per group is two times the square of one point nine six plus zero point eight four, times zero point two five, divided by the effect delta squared.
p_i = exp(z_i)/sum_j exp(z_j): Probability i equals the exponential of score i divided by the sum of exponentials of all scores.
prior_contacts > 2: the number of prior contacts is greater than two
u·v: the dot product of u and v
v_t=beta*v_(t-1)+(1-beta)*g_t: Velocity at step t equals beta times the previous velocity plus one minus beta times the current gradient.
w_new=w-eta*gradient(J): The new weight equals the old weight minus learning rate eta times the gradient of objective J.
w·x+b=0: The dot product of w and x plus bias b equals zero.
x1>0: feature x one is greater than zero
x_t=sqrt(alpha_bar_t)*x_0+sqrt(1-alpha_b: The noisy input at step t is the square root of cumulative alpha times the original input, plus the square root of one minus cumulative alpha times noise epsilon.
y_hat=w·x+b: The predicted target equals the dot product of weights w and inputs x plus bias b.
z=(x-mu)/s: The standardized value z is x minus training mean mu, divided by training standard deviation s.
z=sum_j v_j a_j+b2: The output score z is the sum of output weight j times hidden activation j, plus output bias b two.
z_i = sum_j X_ij w_j + b: The score for row i is the sum over features j of matrix entry X sub i j times weight j, plus scalar bias b.
{text,sources}: an object containing generated text and its sources
||x|| = sqrt(sum_j x_j²): The Euclidean norm of x is the square root of the sum of its squared coordinates.
